# Independent original target-validator captures

All fixtures were generated by unchanged `rust/tools/check_encoder_target.py`.
The initial three corpora predate the native module; later error captures precede
their corresponding native repairs. Source SHA256 is retained in each corpus.

- primitive-original:11 real ELF/AGNOS-loader admission cases, including truncated,
  wrong architecture/class/endian, duplicates, no resolved path, escaping root
  and a missing resolved library.
- run-original:23 complete run histories. Only external command/disk boundaries
  are controlled; original source extraction, file identities, package pins,
  static link group, environment policy, exact packet/trace checks, final hash,
  completed-case prefix and failure/receipt finalization execute unchanged.
- command-original:five command phases. Actual shell success/nonzero and actual
  exec failure preserve binary stdout/stderr and command receipts. Timeout is
  injected at the subprocess boundary with the original300second value; timestamps
  are omitted from captured expected records and checked structurally at runtime.
- log-open-original:two additional captures execute the unchanged original command
  function with a directory obstructing either stdout.bin or stderr.bin. They
  preserve the actual OS error, command receipt, stdout-before-stderr open order
  and proof that the child never starts. Only timestamps and temporary root paths
  are normalized. The test binds the complete capture to SHA256
  `df6a9ef3d585ced45933400e6ad15190b850deaefdd6bf2be27dfb8f58288398`.

Five source cases require packet counts16/16/68/6/6, total112. This is host QEMU
validation using supplied frozen target artifacts and an AGNOS loader; it does
not execute on a device, download/install packages or claim target performance.
Capture scripts/raw temporary evidence remain ignored scratch. Files here are
synthetic source/process captures with no credentials/device/user captures.
Native checker source/bin identities replace the original Python checker record;
all other input hashes, package pins and precise comparison gates are retained.

- raw-hash-cli-original: two real unchanged-original CLI processes with byte
  `ff` in the Rust/JPEG hash argument. Both retain Python surrogateescape text
  in options and create a FAIL receipt at the original hash-validation phase.
  Native regressions compare exact failure payload and decoded codepoints.

The native receipt additionally identifies the executing checker ELF. A real
regression invokes two owned binary copies, appends harmless bytes to one copy,
then requires distinct exact executable hashes with unchanged failure/input
semantics. It never modifies the test runner or a live parent executable.
All 23 full-run cases compare captured failure payloads exactly.

The final host-QEMU proof passed all five cases/112 packets, with 234 identical
trace/packet files across original/native checker runs. The new checker recorded
its executing ELF hash; a bounded build receipt binds 18 policy/manifests/lock
files before/after build. Its final native exec trace contains no Python/PyPy.
Preparation scripts are ignored evidence tooling and are outside that native
execution proof. Host QEMU evidence does not establish device behavior.
